- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) after a spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.4) and price is trending upward, model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) with low sentiment, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a sharp spike, model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of recent prices.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is > 20% above recent 18-day average, flag for downward correction unless sentiment is strong.  
- If sentiment history shows sudden drop after model peak, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “overcorrection” bias.
